instagram_caption:
Satyajit Ray pawned his wife's jewellery to keep filming. 🎞️

In 1952 Ray began shooting his first film, Pather Panchali. He had already borrowed against his insurance policy, and from friends and relatives.

By 1953 the money had run out and shooting stopped for almost a year. Then the chief minister of West Bengal was approached, and the state government agreed to fund the film, paying in instalments.

The film was released in 1955, and Ray kept making films for decades.

In 1992 the Academy gave him an honorary award for his "rare mastery of the art of motion pictures". Too ill to travel, he thanked them on film from a hospital bed in Calcutta. He died 24 days after the ceremony.
